# PolicyGuard small fixture (seed 42)

Generated by `python -m app.ingest.pg_generate --fixture tests/fixtures/pg_small`. Do not edit by hand; regenerate.
The full world (`--out data/policyguard`, 50,000 policyholders, 30 days, all scenarios and the golden set) is gitignored.

**Timestamps are plain UTC with no timezone** (`2026-11-20T18:08:00` = 23:38 IST). Demo day is 2026-11-20.

| File | Rows | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| `agents.json` | 8 agents + 5 branch managers (`role`) | `agents` (`home_city`, `usual_start_hour`/`usual_end_hour` in **IST**, `hr_status`, `credential_enabled`, `manager_id`) |
| `portfolios.jsonl` | 4,000 | `portfolios` (managers own their team's customers) |
| `policyholders.jsonl` | 3,780 | `parties` (`account_id` = `policyholder_id`; `product`, `city` from migration 0012) |
| `claims.jsonl` / `partner_keys.json` | 1,065 / 3 | `partner_claim_assignments` (each claim is assigned to exactly one TPA key) |
| `context_records.json` | 24 | `context_records`: `subject_agent` = whose portfolio or leave, `named_agent` = who it authorises, `valid_from` inclusive / `valid_to` exclusive (naive UTC, IST day bounds); the readable ref (LV-221, TKT-4471) is `payload.ref`, the DB assigns `id` |
| `history.jsonl` | 2,111 | `access_events`: 7 normal days for the 8 agents |
| `scenarios/*.jsonl` | S1, S1b, S1c, S1d, S5 | `access_events` with `labels` (scoring only) and `offset_s` (for replay) |
| `manifest.json` | | counts, and per scenario: actor, expected signals, score, route, verdict |

Event keys: `event_id, ts, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, policyholder_id, tier, records,
outcome, channel, ip, device, city, country, session_id` (+ `detail` on search/export, `labels` and `offset_s` on
scenario events). Load with `python -m app.ingest.pg_load tests/fixtures/pg_small --reset`: `event_id` becomes
`access_events.detail.event_ref` and the database assigns the integer `id`.
Each opened record is one `view` event (records=1); login and search are tier T3 with records=0; the export is
`resource_type` `export_file` with its row count; outcomes are `allowed`, `denied` (403) or `not_found` (404).

| Scenario | Actor | Records | Plan score | Route | Key context |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 bad night | AG-1147 | 1,840 T1 + 1,200-row export | 89 | incident | new device `dv-9f2c`, city Lucknow, 23:38 IST |
| S1b genuine cover | AG-1033 Anita → AG-0932 Priya | 130 T2 | 54 | auto_resolve | `LV-221` by MG-014; `TKT-4471` by MG-014 naming Anita |
| S1c forged ticket | AG-1088 Dev → AG-1090 Raj | 130 T2 | 54 | incident | `TKT-4480` written by Dev himself; no leave |
| S1d forged on real leave | AG-1120 Kiran → AG-1121 Meena | 170 T2 | 55 | incident | `LV-230` is real, but `TKT-4490` is Kiran's own |
| S5 ex-employee | AG-0577 | 40 T2 (own) | 50 → floor 60 | incident | `hr_status` terminated 2026-11-19, `credential_enabled` still true |

Checked when generated: every history view is in the actor's own portfolio; nobody has activity on a leave day; no
servicing assignment, transfer or approval names a scenario subject; the colleagues' p95 daily records (134, 146) are
above the cover volumes, so `check_corroboration` passes only for S1b; recomputing the plan's formula from the data
gives 89 / 54 / 54 / 55 / 49→60.
